agent_priors_used: PRIOR, general caching-systems knowledge, not SPIDER evidence: a cache or compiled artifact pays for itself only above a reuse count that depends on the cost of RE-VALIDATING the cached item, not of producing it. Systems that re-validate cheaply amortize; systems that must re-derive do not. Used to make the break-even reuse count f*, rather than a pass/fail ratio at one chosen reuse count, the primary quantity in the product economics question.

PRIOR, general tool-agent knowledge, not SPIDER evidence: a deterministic compiled executor with no registry, no write path and no staleness surface is the baseline any persistent-memory architecture must beat, because it captures much of the reuse benefit for free. Most published agent-memory work compares against retrieval and instructions rather than against that arm. Used to require a no-memory deterministic-executor arm rather than allowing a comparison only against cold browsing and RAG.

PRIOR, general knowledge about agents and the environment, not SPIDER evidence: where an agent can cheaply re-read a resource, remembering it is a liability rather than an asset, because persistence imports staleness and false-accept risk that the agent did not have to carry. This is the general form of what SPIDER's own real-web packet observed at one site class; I use the prior to generalize and I do not claim SPIDER has established the general result.

PRIOR, general knowledge about long-horizon agents, not SPIDER evidence: a memory that silently replays a wrong action injects error at roughly the rate it removes work, so error propagation is a first-class term in any economics claim and an abstention/false-accept measurement is not optional decoration. Used to make a mandatory abstention arm part of the product question rather than an optional secondary metric.

PRIOR, general research-program knowledge, not SPIDER evidence: in a large autonomous program the dominant failure mode is instrument invalidity and unbanked substrate, not shortage of hypotheses, so the marginal value of one more mechanism packet is usually below the marginal value of repairing the instrument contract. Used to ratify Physics on a certification battery and Runtime on a substrate other lanes can cite, even though neither is a mechanism discovery.

PRIOR, general research-program knowledge, not SPIDER evidence: the correct response to many consecutive packets of one kind is a change of substrate or a change of level of description, not a better estimator on the same substrate. Used to treat the C-WEB-DYNAMICS synthetic generator as a parked program rather than a continuing thread, and to prefer Frontier's surface measurement over a seventeenth transfer packet.

PRIOR, general knowledge about planning horizons, not SPIDER evidence: preconditions that are cheaper to satisfy after the fact than to declare up front are systematically declared generously and then fail at freeze time, which is how a program accumulates unfireable gates. Used to require, on every allocation this cycle, that each frozen threshold be shown arithmetically reachable at the declared sample size and that each control be shown capable of firing or failing, before freeze rather than after.

PRIOR, general knowledge about research systems, not SPIDER evidence: an inherited handoff is a local optimum detector, not an oracle, and a lane that has run out of local questions usually has not run out of program-level questions. Used as the procedure for the cognitive reset on all six lanes, in particular to prefer neglected product-central claims over the claim a lane most recently touched.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment:
PROGRAM STATE. 406 canonical experiments, 90 lane-listed recent experiments, and no claim above EXPERIMENTAL. C-MEAS-VALID, C-PARAM-INHERIT and C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY sit at EXPERIMENTAL; every other claim is at HYPOTHESIS; nothing is VALIDATED, PRODUCT_CORE or SHIPPED. The dominant failure mode is not a shortage of ideas, it is instrument and control-plane invalidity: 59 of the 90 lane-listed recent decisions begin with MEASUREMENT_INVALID and 42 of 90 independent audits return MEASUREMENT_INVALID. I verified two facts directly in committed code and they dominate this cycle's direction.

(1) THE SHIPPED PRODUCT CANNOT INHERIT ANYTHING IT DISCOVERS. At main HEAD, src/spider/kernel.py distill() hard-codes confidence=0.5 (line 90) while resolve() requires confidence >= min_confidence=0.8 (line 114) and separately requires exact intent string equality (line 97). No distillation path in the shipped kernel can therefore return EXECUTABLE, and no paraphrased goal can ever resolve. The only parameterized path exercised in tests/test_kernel.py hand-builds a Mechanism at confidence 0.95 and upserts it directly. This independently reproduces the recorded 0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions (EXP-FRONTIER-36249071934). Consequence: every economics result this program has produced so far describes a capability the product does not have, and the last product verdict already recorded the same thing - durability unmeasured, committed delta scheduled for revert. Fixing that is a precondition for any external-agent claim, not a nice-to-have.

(2) A PROGRAM-WIDE CONTROL-PLANE DEFECT IS DESTROYING PACKETS. scripts/freeze_experiment.py writes exactly three hashes (request.json, spec.json, prereg.md; lines 79-82) and scripts/check_scope.py grants DESIGN an empty code-prefix list (line 124). Any frozen gate of the form 'code hashed into freeze.json' or 'code bound via preregistration' is therefore unsatisfiable in every lane. The Codex attributes the loss of three consecutive C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE packets to exactly this, the last of them while being falsely attested PASS. Smallest next action, which I cannot take because it is a control-plane code change outside this role's write scope: either extend freeze_experiment.py to hash a code manifest that DESIGN may declare, or permanently retire code-bound gates in favour of EXECUTE-stage sha256 attestation. Until one of those happens I impose it as a standing condition on every allocation below, and I refuse to let a fourth packet die of it.

THE SCIENTIFIC CENTRE HAS ALSO MOVED, opposite to the recent history. All 49 C-CROSSSITE events asked whether a mechanism transfers to a held-out site. None asked whether there is anything to transfer. The one packet that actually reached real websites answered that upstream question by accident: 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, no write verb, and identifiers a fresh episode re-reads cheaply. Combined with the valid finding that a within-episode scratchpad closed 100 percent of residual novelty at 48.0 units against cross-episode compiled at 48.2 and a no-memory deterministic executor at 40.94 against a 38.6 threshold (EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510), the program now holds a live, decision-grade threat to its own central premise: on the accessible substrate class, persistent cross-episode state may be superfluous, and the honest competitor is re-derivation plus caching. SPIDER has never measured the break-even reuse count at which persistence pays for itself net of distillation, verification, guard and maintenance. That is the question I give Product, posed in two regimes, because the sign of the answer depends on the regime and the regime is the thing we do not know.

director_mandate.scout_assessment:
The brief was treated as staff advice and changed three of my six decisions, was overruled on four points, and contributed no external finding as SPIDER evidence.

WHAT I ACCEPTED. (a) The external landscape section's central observation - that SPIDER has never been tested against any published memory-augmented web agent, and that Agent Workflow Memory, WebCoach and ReasoningBank all report gains from exactly the mechanism SPIDER claims - is a real and unflattering gap, and it is the reason Intel's question now includes a bounded external performance envelope read from published results rather than only a cost-accounting convention. (b) The brief's local-attractor diagnosis for Frontier agrees with the snapshot's tunnel flag (12 of 15 frontier experiments on C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY, ceiling 21/40 = 0.525) and I acted on it by terminating that bounded thread and ratifying the pivot off it. (c) The brief is right that C-MEAS-VALID's ceiling is narrow; I used that fact to keep Runtime on the substrate that unblocks other lanes rather than to widen its validation breadth, which is a different response than the one proposed.

WHAT I DECLINED. (a) TERMINATE physics on synthetic DGPs. The constitution forbids closing a domain on a failed bounded program, and physics' live thread is the certification instrument without which no later C-WEB-DYNAMICS question about the Web rather than a generator is decidable. I recorded the synthetic program as PARKED, not terminated, and the synthetic-DGP sub-thread is explicitly not continued. (b) Expand C-MEAS-VALID to production OAuth/OIDC and CDN/load-balancer robustness. No live experiment in the Codex is blocked on the absence of an OIDC server; the blocked experiments are blocked on missing writable controls or an uncertified instrument, and this route adds unprovisioned infrastructure, which is the specific failure that has cost this lane many cycles. (c) Allocate a dedicated C-LLM-INHERIT experiment with an external browser agent on a real benchmark this cycle. It presupposes a model credential the Codex already records as absent (EXP-PRODUCT-35651924708, 0 of 120 executions, BLOCKED), a browser stack whose find_spec the frontier lineage records as None, and a kernel that can execute inherited mechanisms, which the committed code provably cannot. Sequencing it now would buy a fifth consecutive non-decision on a live claim; I have instead recorded the credential as the smallest next action. (d) Reproduce Agent Workflow Memory or WebCoach as baselines inside a lane. Same credential problem, and reproduction is a multi-cycle engineering effort; reading published reported numbers under a frozen identity gate yields most of the decision content at a fraction of the cost, which is what I assigned.

WHERE THE BRIEF CONFLICTS WITH THE CODEX, I FOLLOWED THE CODEX. The brief states that Graph is 'blocked on parameter-slot-count tie-break (7 consecutive BLOCKED experiments)' and recommends pivoting Graph for that reason. The Codex does not support this: C-PARAM-INHERIT shows 3 BLOCKED events in 56 and C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE shows none at all; the recorded Graph losses are MEASUREMENT_INVALID traceable to an unsatisfiable V9 code-bound gate and to unfireable thresholds, not to a slot-count tie-break. The claim that is genuinely blocked in volume is C-DELTA-REPAIR (5 BLOCKED in 12), which the brief does not flag. I therefore set Graph's direction on the verified neglect of C-FRESHNESS (61 events, 1 in the recent window, last decision MEASUREMENT_INVALID, and its three former blockers all resolved in accepted evidence) rather than on the brief's stated cause, and I note the discrepancy here because the distinction changes what a fix would have to be. I also did not accept the brief's 'C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE EXPERIMENTAL' framing as a promotion: the effective registry status is HYPOTHESIS and the last three events are MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

I spent no part of this cycle on browsing or literature review, and no external finding in the brief is treated as SPIDER evidence anywhere in this allocation.
